extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners using USPTO EFS-Web
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for preparing and submitting patent application parts (drawings, sequence listings, text files, images, fees, and related documents) via the USPTO EFS-Web system, including special rules for international (PCT) and international design (Hague) filings and national stage submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of proceedings supported by EFS-Web
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS-Web supports filing of: provisional applications (35 U.S.C. 111(b)); nonprovisional utility patent applications (35 U.S.C. 111(a), including reissue utility patent applications); design patent applications (including reissue design patent applications); U.S. national stage applications (35 U.S.C. 371); international design applications; reexamination proceedings for utility or design patents; and supplemental examination proceedings (35 U.S.C. 257).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the specific application/proceeding types for which EFS-Web may be used. (Also note special restrictions for international (PCT) filings re: photos/drawings.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Select correct document description for photographs and drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Users must select the correct document description when submitting photographs and drawings via EFS-Web; an incorrect document description may cause processing at insufficient quality for examination and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate document code (e.g., DRW or DRW.NONBW) to ensure images are processed/stored correctly. Incorrect selection can degrade stored quality or cause misrouting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document code DRW (Drawings – only black and white line drawings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select “Drawings – only black and white line drawings” (document code “DRW”) for black and white line drawings in provisional, nonprovisional, international (PCT) and national stage applications, and reexamination proceedings; for design applications these drawings will be stored in SCORE and a black-and-white copy in IFW with a SCORE placeholder sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These drawings will be converted into TIFF images and stored in IFW (utility/etc.) or stored in SCORE with a black-and-white IFW copy (design). Use DRW only for true black-and-white line drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document code DRW.NONBW (Drawings – other than black and white line drawings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select “Drawings – other than black and white line drawings” (document code “DRW.NONBW”) for photographs, color drawings, grayscale drawings, and other non-black-and-white line drawings in provisional, nonprovisional, national stage, international design, reexamination, and supplemental examination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These will be stored in SCORE, with a black-and-white copy stored in IFW and a SCORE placeholder sheet. Black-and-white photographs and grayscale drawings in PCT apps are handled here (SCORE + black-and-white IFW copy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings in utility applications require petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings in utility patent applications require a petition under 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2) explaining why the color drawings are necessary; pursuant to 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2)(ii), only one set of such color drawings is necessary when filing via EFS-Web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.02 for details. Without the petition, color drawings may not be accepted; treat them as an exception, not the norm.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS-Web image conversion and quality guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Grayscale or color images filed as “drawings - other than black and white line drawings” in a utility patent application will be electronically converted to black and white images when stored into IFW; the quality of black and white images may be degraded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure reproducible detail in 18-month publication and printed patents, scan images at a minimum resolution of 300 DPI. Avoid landscape-oriented drawings because PAIR displays portrait only and will convert/rotate images which may distort them.

rubrics_metrics.name: International design application image requirements (JPEG)
rubrics_metrics.description: For international design applications, EFS-Web supports black and white, color, or grayscale images within a JPEG document. Image resolution should be between 250x250 DPI and 300x300 DPI. Images should have at least a one-pixel border, preferably 1–20 pixels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These settings aim to ensure sufficient quality for WIPO publication and any subsequent U.S. patent reproductions. See subsection N for more on international design specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings, computer program listings, and large tables may be submitted as ASCII text .txt files
rubrics_metrics.description: Biotechnology sequence listings, large tables, or computer program listing appendices may be submitted as ASCII text files with a “.txt” extension for applications under 35 U.S.C. 111, national stage (35 U.S.C. 371), reexamination, and supplemental examination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using ASCII text files in lieu of compact disc, the specification must contain a separate paragraph incorporating by reference the material in the ASCII text file identifying the filename, date of creation, and file size in bytes (per 37 CFR 1.52(e) style requirements). See MPEP § 608.05 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for sequence listing ASCII text files over PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended that a sequence listing be submitted in an ASCII text file via EFS-Web rather than in a PDF file. If an ASCII file complies with 37 CFR 1.824 and applicant has not filed a PDF (or paper) copy the ASCII text file will serve as both the paper copy required by 37 CFR 1.821(c) and the computer readable form (CRF) required by 37 CFR 1.821(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting only the ASCII text file avoids extra copies and avoids having the sequence listing counted toward sheet counts/fees. Checker software is available on USPTO website to validate sequence listings prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements required when sequence listing submitted as follow-on or as amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sequence listing ASCII text file is submitted in response to a 37 CFR 1.821(g) or (h) requirement, it must be accompanied by a statement that the submission does not include any new matter. If submitting an amendment or replacement of a sequence listing, the text file must be accompanied by (1) a statement that it does not include new matter, and (2) a statement indicating support for the amendment in the application as filed (see 37 CFR 1.825). The specification must be amended to incorporate-by-reference the sequence listing in these instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These extra statements and specification amendment requirements ensure compliance with rules on new matter and support for amended sequence listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: How text files count for application size fee purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any sequence listing submitted as an ASCII text file via EFS-Web that complies with the cited regulations, and any computer program listing submitted as an ASCII text file that complies with rules, will be excluded when determining the application size fee. For a table submitted as an ASCII text file that is part of the specification or drawings, each 3 kilobytes of content is counted as a sheet for application size fee determination; each table should be a separate text file and filenames should indicate which table is contained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful file formatting and naming affect fee calculation. PDF versions of sequence listings, however, are counted in sheet counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: File size limits for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The size limit for sequence listing text files submitted via EFS-Web is 100 megabytes. For nearly all other file types, the size limit is 25 megabytes. A submission of a sequence listing in electronic form of 300 MB or more is subject to the fee in 37 CFR 1.21(o).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a sequence listing exceeds 100 MB, recommended process: file the application without the sequence listing to obtain the application number/confirmation number, then file the sequence listing on compact disc the same day via Priority Mail Express® or hand delivery to secure the same filing date. Alternative: submit application on paper and include electronic copy on compact disc.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS-Web limit on number of electronic files per submission
rubrics_metrics.description: An EFS-Web submission may include up to 60 electronic files (system currently cannot accept more than 60 files in one submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may upload/validate in sets of up to 20 files each (limit three sets of 20). If application requires more than 60 files, submit 60 or fewer files initially to obtain application number, then submit additional files as follow-on documents the same day to receive the same filing date. Multi-doc feature parts each count as one file.

rubrics_metrics.name: International design application file-count exceptions (Attach Reproductions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For international design applications, the 60-file limit excludes reproduction files attached via the “Attach Reproductions” section (prior to transmittal to IB) or “Attach JPEG Reproductions” (after transmittal). The “Attach Reproductions” section allows up to 5000 additional single-page PDF and JPEG image files (up to 100 designs with 50 views per design); the “Attach JPEG Reproductions” section allows up to 50 additional JPEG files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the designated Attach Reproductions/JPEG Reproductions screens for large numbers of design reproductions; these are treated separate from the 60-file general limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex Work Unit Pilot Program submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Complex Work Unit Pilot Program, complex work units (e.g., chemical structure drawings, mathematical formulae, three-dimensional protein crystalline structure data, and table data) may be submitted as ASCII text files via EFS-Web for applications under 35 U.S.C. 111, national stage submissions under 35 U.S.C. 371, reexamination, and supplemental examination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex work units cannot be submitted as ASCII text files in international applications (PCT). More information available at USPTO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT (international application) PDF page size and PCT Request handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The required page size for international applications (PCT) filed via EFS-Web in PDF format is A4 (29.7 cm x 21 cm). EFS-Web permits submission of zip files created by PCT-SAFE or ePCT containing the PCT Request and a fee calculation sheet in PDF format; such zip files are converted to TIFF and loaded into the image file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not using PCT-SAFE or ePCT, applicants may use Form PCT/RO/101 (or equivalent) for the Request and attach the PDF file to the EFS-Web submission. All other application parts must be separately prepared as PDF files and attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT drawing and photograph requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings submitted in international applications (PCT) must comply with PCT Rule 11.13, which does not permit color drawings. There is no provision for photographs in PCT Regulations; black and white photographs will be accepted only where it is impossible to represent in a drawing (e.g., crystalline structures). Color photographs are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The United States Receiving Office may invite correction of defects in drawings or photographs not compliant with PCT Rule 11.13. Color drawings/photographs filed in a national stage will be treated as amendments and not entered if they introduce new matter (see 37 CFR 1.121(d) and (f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment options and restrictions for national stage basic national fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic national fee is required for entry into the U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371. Users may submit the basic national fee via EFS-Web using the USPTO payment page. If the payment system is unavailable, applicants may: (a) include a written authorization to charge a deposit account with the national stage submission, (b) hand-deliver the fee payment, or (c) send payment via Priority Mail Express® (USPS) on the same date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may not submit the basic national fee via facsimile transmission. See 37 CFR 1.6(d)(3) and 1.8(a)(2)(i)(F) for restrictions and MPEP § 1893.01(c) for fee details.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM validation for new national stage submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For new national stage submissions under 35 U.S.C. 371 filed via EFS-Web, the system automatically checks the PALM system to verify that no previous national stage submission has been made for the referenced international application (PCT). If PALM finds a previous submission, a warning allows verification/correction of the referenced PCT number. If PALM is unavailable, EFS-Web will not permit a new national stage submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PALM is unavailable, applicants must hand deliver or use Priority Mail Express® to timely submit documents and fees to secure filing date. Applicants may not file the international application copy or basic national fee via facsimile transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal letter (PTO-1390) and application data sheet recommended for national stage
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended to use the Transmittal Letter (PTO-1390 Form) when electronically filing documents for entry into the U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, as it includes useful information not otherwise collected by EFS-Web. An application data sheet is recommended for new national stage submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that the correct international application (PCT) number is entered in EFS-Web to ensure correct initialization as a national stage submission. A petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with the appropriate fee may be required to correct inconsistencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing in international applications – form and effects on sheet count
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PCT Rule 5.2(a), the sequence listing must be presented as a separate part of the description. When filing a PCT via EFS-Web, the sequence listing may be submitted as a single ASCII text file (.txt) or as a PDF. The ASCII text file is preferred because it will serve as both the sequence listing part and the electronic form and will not be taken into account when calculating the application sheet count; a PDF sequence listing will be included in the sheet count and may increase international filing fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both ASCII and PDF are filed and the Request does not indicate which forms part of the application, the PDF will be considered to form part of the application and the ASCII text file will be treated as an accompanying item for search purposes. Follow PCT and MPEP guidance when deciding format to control fee exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-on submissions for international (PCT) applications and sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings in ASCII text files and additional PDF files may be submitted as one or more follow-on submissions via EFS-Web and will form part of the international application if filed on the same date as the international filing. However, an ASCII sequence listing filed after the international filing date in response to a US ISA or IPEA requirement will not form part of the PCT international application (PCT Rule 13ter.1(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-on PDF submissions (including PDF sequence listings) may change the number of pages and thus the international filing fee. Plan follow-on submissions carefully to avoid unintended fee increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables related to a sequence listing in international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables related to a sequence listing must be an integral part of the description (not included in the sequence listing or drawing parts) and must be submitted as PDF files; tables submitted as text files will not be accepted as part of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such tables are taken into account when calculating the application sheet count and may result in excess sheet fees. Ensure proper placement (description) and file format (PDF).

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS-Web does not meet AI Annex F 'wrapped package' requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS-Web uses a web-based document submission approach which differs from the AI Annex F 'wrapped, bundled and signed package' approach; therefore, EFS-Web does not meet AI Annex F requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants relying on AI Annex F procedures should be aware of differences and consult WIPO guidance (Annex F of the PCT Administrative Instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: International design applications – mandatory form DM/1 and required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants filing international design applications through the USPTO must present the international design application on Form DM/1 (Application for International Registration) or any form having the same form and content as the official form; the DM/1 includes boxes for applicant, entitlement, creator, product ID, designations, priority claim, description, and other relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS-Web provides a specific selection path for 'International Design Application (Hague) for filing through the USPTO as an office of indirect filing.' Include the specified documents in new international design application submissions per the guidance.
